newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices fall before payrolls.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices fall before payrolls.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices dropped around 3/4 of a point in late trade on Thursday, hurt by profit-taking ahead of Friday's payrolls data, which in the past has triggered sharp reactions.

"It (the municipal market) is a difficult market to hedge, and because of the threat that if governments get hit with a bad number tomorrow, all the gains you accumulated in the last month could be gone in a day or two (prices fell)," a trader said.
While municipal bonds did not drop as steeply as the benchmark U.S. Treasuries, traders noted that munis also have lagged the benchmark securities in their recent rally.

The rather large volume of new municipal issues sold this week also weighed on prices, though traders said underwriters were helped by the timing of the market's retreat, as many offerings were placed before prices turned down sharply.

As on Wednesday, institutional customers displayed considerable interest in selling bonds, but traders said that if they wanted to get acceptable bids, they largely were forced to offer fairly attractive bonds.
"If you wanted to sell something, you had to sell a little bit of quality that people were looking for," one said.
For example, few full coupon bonds with short calls were being advertized for sale, he added.
But traders said that most of this week's deals appeared to have gone fairly smoothly, even though the market now seemed to have a negative bias ahead of Friday's payrolls report for November.
A consensus survey of Reuter economist forecast that the economy only added 179,000 jobs, down from October's increase of 210,000, and look for the unemployment rate to steady at 5.2 percent.

March U.S. Treasury futures on the Chicago Board of Trade fell 40 ticks to 114-3/32, while the March municipal bond futures lost 33 ticks to 116-9/32. The MOB spread fattened to plus 70 ticks, a rise of around 20 ticks from levels seen early this week.
The Reuters 10-year tax-exempt general obligation bond index rose three basis points from last week to 4.82 percent.
In the secondary market, active issues included Chicago Illinois Skyway Toll Bridge Revenues of January 2023, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, and were bid at 5.63 percent NET, up two basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Community Revenues of June 2027, which have a coupon of 5-3/8 percent, were bid at 5.69 percent NET, up one basis point.
